transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-08
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Pinecrest CISO), Laura Kim (VP Eng), Sofia Martinez (Cloud Architect)

Summary: quick security posture discovery. Pinecrest is evaluating Redwood for patient-facing summarization and triage features; primary concerns: SOC2/ISO compliance, SSO/SAML with Okta, RBAC to limit model access, audit logging/retention for PHI-adjacent logs, and encryption/KMS integration. They are leaning towards dedicated or private because of regulatory controls but want to understand hosted tradeoffs and whether Redwood can support required controls (customer-managed keys, VPC peering, on-prem option).

00:00:12 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick intros?
00:00:20 Raj Patel: hey, Raj here, CISO at Pinecrest. We're mainly responsible for security and compliance and will be driving the vendor assessments.
00:00:28 Laura Kim: Laura, VP Eng, we'll be owning the integration and day-to-day infra.
00:00:33 Devon Park: Devon, Solutions Eng at Redwood - I'll cover the technical bits and deployment options.
00:00:39 Sofia Martinez: Sofia, cloud architect, I'll be doing the network and KMS mapping.

00:01:05 Maya Chen: Cool. Quick context - you're building triage and summarization for patient messages, correct? That means sensitive data, potential PHI. Can you confirm what data types flow to the model and whether you need HIPAA-level controls?
00:01:22 Raj Patel: Yes so it's patient messages and clinical notes, mostly identifiers plus free text. We're in exploratory stage, but security team treats this as high. We need SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 is a plus. Also strict retention and the ability for key management and isolating logs.
00:01:42 Devon Park: Right so for Redwood Hosted we offer SOC 2 Type II and can do customer-managed key support for encryption at rest in our Dedicated/Private offerings. The hosted API can be configured with strict retention settings and we do produce audit logs - but, I mean, for PHI many customers prefer Dedicated or Private for extra isolation and VPC peering.
00:02:05 Laura Kim: Can you clarify the difference between Dedicated and Private in terms of network isolation and control plane? We want to know if Redwood still has access to logs or control plane data.
00:02:18 Devon Park: Sure. Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool in our cloud tenant but isolated per-customer - you get dedicated capacity and some network rules; Redwood still runs the control plane and manages the service, but we can restrict access and provide tenant-level audit logs. Private is a VPC or on-prem deployment where the control plane can be customer-managed; in that case you control KMS and we only have management plane access as agreed in the contract.
00:02:45 Raj Patel: So Private means our keys never leave our KMS?
00:02:50 Devon Park: With Private, yes - you can use your own KMS or HSM; the service can be configured so that key material never leaves your boundary. For Dedicated we offer a bring-your-key model where you control keys via KMS integrations but the runtime may still communicate with Redwood-managed control plane for billing and updates.
00:03:12 Sofia Martinez: Ok, Id like specifics: which KMS providers, what's the auth flow for SAML/SSO, how logs are shipped, retention windows?
00:03:22 Devon Park: We support AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and common HSM integrations for Private. For SSO we integrate via SAML/OIDC - Okta, Azure AD are common. RBAC supports role mappings so you can limit model invocation to certain roles. Audit logs can be streamed to customer S3 or GCS buckets for Dedicated/Private; retention we can configure, default at 90 days but can be extended per enterprise plan.
00:03:53 Raj Patel: default 90 days isn't going to cut it - we need 7 years for some audit trails for regulatory reasons.
00:03:59 Maya Chen: Right - we've seen customers request long-term retention; we can ship logs to the customer's own storage and you can keep them as long as you need. We'll include that in the doc packet.
00:04:12 Laura Kim: What about redaction? We don't want raw PHI stored in logs if possible.
00:04:18 Devon Park: We have configurable log scrubbing and PII redaction rules at the ingestion layer. There's also the option to only record metadata to the audit trail and keep transcript payloads ephemeral - in Private deployments you can enforce policies so full payloads never persist in Redwood-managed storage.
00:04:39 Raj Patel: Encryption at rest - if Redwood holds the disks for Dedicated, is data encrypted with keys we control?
00:04:47 Devon Park: For Dedicated we support CMEK-style integrations where you provide KMS keys; the disks are encrypted using your keys. For Hosted (shared) we use provider-managed encryption and SOC 2 controls, but CMEK isn't generally available on the fully shared tier.
00:05:02 Sofia Martinez: Any certifications we can review right now? SOC 2 report, ISO certs?
00:05:08 Maya Chen: Yes - we have a SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO readiness checklist. I'll share the SOC 2 redacted report after NDA.
00:05:18 Raj Patel: NDA first?
00:05:20 Maya Chen: Yes, we'll put the NDA on DocuSign, I can send that today.
00:05:25 Laura Kim: Great.

00:06:05 Raj Patel: About SSO - we use Okta. Can you map SAML role assertions into Redwood RBAC and restrict model access per team?
00:06:15 Devon Park: Yep. We map SAML groups to role bindings. You can have roles like model-invoke, admin, auditor. You can also limit which models a role can call - useful if you want to allow dev to call smaller models and restrict production models to a narrower set.
00:06:33 Laura Kim: Does RBAC extend to API keys and service accounts?
00:06:37 Devon Park: Yes, we have service principals with scoped tokens. Service accounts can be limited to routes and model versions, and we log all token usage in the audit trail.

00:07:08 Sofia Martinez: Network - we run in AWS. For Private we can do VPC peering or private link?
00:07:15 Devon Park: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink-style connectivity depending on region. For Dedicated we offer VPC peering against a customer-managed VPC; for Private on-prem you'd run an appliance or containerized runtime behind your network.
00:07:32 Raj Patel: For data residency, we need all inference to stay in us-east-1. Is that configurable?
00:07:38 Devon Park: Yes, region pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted tenants can route to region-specific endpoints but data in shared hosted tiers may be in multiple AZs; we can discuss guaranteed residency in the contract.

00:08:05 Laura Kim: What about model artifacts - are they stored centrally? If we fine-tune or upload model snapshots, who controls them?
00:08:15 Devon Park: Model artifacts uploaded to Dedicated or Private instances remain in your tenant storage; access is governed by RBAC. For Hosted, models in our catalog are managed by Redwood and we maintain versioning and rollback, but you can restrict access and treat them as private model spaces with encryption.

00:08:46 Raj Patel: Auditability question: can we get immutable logs for admin actions and inference calls? Also chain-of-custody for model changes?
00:08:57 Devon Park: We produce append-only audit logs with timestamps and cryptographic integrity checks if needed; for Private you can integrate with your SIEM and send logs to a write-once storage. Model change events and rollouts are captured in the console and can be exported as part of the audit trail.

00:09:32 Raj Patel: Are you SOC 2 controls mapped to CIS or NIST? We map vendor controls to NIST 800-53 so we need control mappings.
00:09:41 Maya Chen: We have a compliance matrix mapping SOC 2 to NIST and ISO controls - I will include that in the packet.

00:10:05 Laura Kim: Let's talk about retention and deletion: if a user requests data deletion under HIPAA/other privacy laws, can we delete logs and cached KV payloads?
00:10:16 Devon Park: Yes - we support programmatic deletion of user data and cache invalidation. For Dedicated/Private we can guarantee deletion from Redwood-managed storage; for Private you control data, so you can purge as you see fit. We also support TTLs for KV cache to limit retention.

00:11:02 Raj Patel: Latency and fallback policies - if we use Hosted but need to fail over, do we get degraded models or queueing? Concern is PHI shouldn't route to a lower-compliance endpoint if a region goes down.
00:11:18 Devon Park: We have smart routing policies - you can restrict fallback to only compatible models within same compliance posture or region. For strict regulatory setups, we recommend Dedicated/Private and configured fallbacks that never cross compliance boundaries.

00:12:00 Sofia Martinez: For encryption in transit, are you TLS1.3 and do you support mutual TLS for service-to-service?
00:12:07 Devon Park: TLS 1.3 by default, and Mutual TLS is supported for Private and can be arranged for Dedicated.

00:12:40 Raj Patel: Can we do penetration testing or security assessments?
00:12:44 Maya Chen: Yes, we can accommodate customer pentests under a coordinated process; we'll need to schedule and sign the right agreements. There are blackout windows and a point of contact.

00:13:20 Laura Kim: How about data exfiltration prevention - do you scan responses or have output filters?
00:13:28 Devon Park: We have output filters and response policies that can redact or block certain output patterns; for sensitive PHI flows we recommend a post-processing layer on your side as well.

00:14:05 Raj Patel: Team question: who will have access to logs inside Redwood? Is there an internal access policy and how do you audit staff access?
00:14:15 Maya Chen: Redwood has strict internal access controls, privileged access is limited and audited; we can provide details in the SOC 2 and in a minimal access listing.

00:14:40 Dev (interruption, crosstalk): sorry, did you say 3rd-party subprocessor list?
00:14:45 Raj Patel: yes we need subprocessors and data flows.
00:14:48 Devon Park: We maintain a subprocessor list and can provide a DPA that enumerates subprocessors and flow diagrams.

00:15:12 Raj Patel: Ok high-level timeline - we aim to pilot in Q3, production by year-end. Our blockers are legal (DPA), SOC 2 review, technical pilot for VPC, and pricing.
00:15:28 Maya Chen: That aligns with typical customers. We'll send the SOC 2 and DPA, and Devon will run a VPC pilot plan.

00:16:02 Laura Kim: Security-specific concern: can you support a locked-down model that doesn't allow internet egress from runtime? We need to prevent external calls from inference nodes.
00:16:12 Devon Park: Yes, Private and Dedicated can be configured with no internet egress - outbound network policies can be locked down to internal endpoints and customer-controlled telemetry sinks.

00:16:40 Raj Patel: About billing and logs: we need token-level visibility to reconcile cost to logs for audits.
00:16:48 Devon Park: We provide token-level cost breakdowns in Redwood Console and can export per-request traces that map to billing lines.

00:17:20 Sofia Martinez: For key rotation, how is downtime handled if keys rotate?
00:17:26 Devon Park: We support key rotation with seamless rewrap - you can rotate keys with minimal disruption; in Private you control rotation and we provide a handshake flow to avoid downtime.

00:18:02 Raj Patel: If we do Dedicated, what's the SLA and how is incident response handled for security incidents?
00:18:09 Maya Chen: Dedicated has SLA options (uptime, latency) in enterprise contracts; incident response is handled by our security team and we provide notifications and a post-mortem. We'll include our incident response playbook redacted for initial review.

00:18:50 Laura Kim: Are there limits on model fine-tuning or custom data for Hosted? We want to ensure training data doesn't leak across tenants.
00:18:59 Devon Park: Fine-tuning on Hosted is scoped per-tenant; we cluster by tenant and maintain isolation. For strict isolation we recommend Dedicated/Private where fine-tune artifacts remain in tenant storage.

00:19:30 Raj Patel: Any known gaps in your compliance posture we should be aware of?
00:19:36 Maya Chen: We're SOC 2 Type II audited; ISO 27001 certification is in progress, expected later this year. We'll note any control gaps in the compliance matrix we share.

00:20:05 Laura Kim: Ok, let's talk practical next steps and responsibilities.
00:20:12 Maya Chen: Proposed next steps: 1) We'll send NDA and SOC 2 report; 2) Devon will schedule VPC technical deep dive and provide required network ports and diagrams; 3) Sophie/Sofia will share retention policy and sample dataset; 4) we'll provide draft pricing for Dedicated pilot.
00:20:34 Raj Patel: Good. Also can we get threat model examples for healthcare workloads?
00:20:40 Devon Park: Yes - we'll share a redacted threat model and some recommended mitigations.

00:21:10 Raj Patel: A couple of quick clarifications: will Redwood sign BAAs for HIPAA?
00:21:17 Maya Chen: Yes - Redwood signs BAAs for customers processing PHI; we'll route that through legal after the NDA.
00:21:26 Raj Patel: Perfect.

00:22:05 Laura Kim: Any additional docs for SAML setup for Okta?
00:22:09 Devon Park: We'll send SAML integration guide with example metadata and attribute mappings.

00:22:40 Raj Patel: About the pilot, we want to run synthetic benchmarks with representative messages and measure QPS and latency at 100ms p99 target - is that feasible?
00:22:51 Devon Park: Absolutely. For Dedicated we can set up a benchmark harness and provide baseline numbers; we'll need your sample data and the exact prompts. We can also run a dry-run on Hosted to validate scale.
00:23:30 Maya Chen: Any final concerns?
00:23:36 Raj Patel: Mainly: keys, retention, DPA, and proof of auditability.
00:23:43 Maya Chen: Understood. We'll include all evidence and next steps.

00:24:10 Transcript quality note: auto-transcribed, some names or acronyms may be misrecognized (e.g., KV cache, KMS, VPCed).

00:25:00 Closing recap (approx):
- Deliverables: NDA + SOC 2 + compliance matrix (Maya)
- Technical deliverables: VPC deep dive + ports/diagram + pilot plan + threat model (Devon)
- Customer deliverables: retention policy + sample dataset (Sofia)
- Timeline: pilot planning in next 2 weeks, pilot Q3, production by year-end

00:26:20 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone; I'll send notes and the SOC 2 link once the NDA is in place.
00:26:28 Raj Patel: Thanks, talk soon.

[call ends]
